exercises.heading: 3.9. Exercises

list.item: If $$V$$ is the volume of a cube with edge length $$x$$ and the cube expands as time passes, find $$dV \slash dt$$ in terms of $$\mathit{dx} \slash dt$$ .
If the length of the edge of a cube is increasing at a rate of $$4{cm} \slash s$$ , how fast is the volume of the cube increasing when the edge length is $$15$$ cm?
If $$A$$ is the area of a circle with radius $$r$$ and the circle expands as time passes, find $$dA \slash dt$$ in terms of $$dr \slash dt$$ .

Suppose oil spills from a ruptured tanker and spreads in a circular pattern. If the radius of the oil spill increases at a constant rate of $$2{m \slash s}$$ , how fast is the area of the spill increasing when the radius is $$30$$ m?

problem.paragraph: Each side of a square is increasing at a rate of $$6{{cm} \slash s}$$ . At what rate is the area of the square increasing when the area of the square is $$16{cm}^{2}$$ ?
The radius of a sphere is increasing at a rate of $$4{mm} \slash s$$ . How fast is the volume increasing when the diameter is $$80$$ mm?
The radius of a spherical ball is increasing at a rate of $$2{cm} \slash \min$$ . At what rate is the surface area of the ball increasing when the radius is $$8$$ cm?

The length of a rectangle is increasing at a rate of $$8{{cm} \slash s}$$ and its width is increasing at a rate of $$3{{cm} \slash s}$$ . When the length is $$20$$ cm and the width is $$10$$ cm, how fast is the area of the rectangle increasing?
A cylindrical tank with radius $$5$$ m is being filled with water at a rate of $$3m^{3} \slash \min$$ . How fast is the height of the water increasing?
The area of a triangle with sides of lengths $$a$$ and $$b$$ and contained angle $$\theta$$ is $$A = \frac{1}{2}ab\sin\theta$$ (See Formula 6 in Appendix D.)

list.item: If $$a = 2$$ cm, $$b = 3$$ cm, and $$\theta$$ increases at a rate of $$0.2{rad} \slash \min$$ , how fast is the area increasing when $$\theta = \pi \slash 3$$ ?

If $$a = 2$$ cm, $$b$$ increases at a rate of $$1.5{cm} \slash \min$$ , and $$\theta$$ increases at a rate of $$0.2{rad} \slash \min$$ , how fast is the area increasing when $$b = 3$$ cm and $$\theta = \pi \slash 3$$ ?

If $$a$$ increases at a rate of $$2.5{cm} \slash \min$$ , $$b$$ increases at a rate of $$1.5{cm} \slash \min$$ , and $$\theta$$ increases at a rate of $$0.2{rad} \slash \min$$ , how fast is the area increasing when $$a = 2$$ cm, $$b = 3$$ cm, and $$\theta = \pi \slash 3$$ ?

problem.paragraph: Suppose $$4x^{2} + 9y^{2} = 25$$ , where $$x$$ and $$y$$ are functions of $$t$$ .

list.item: If $$\mathit{dy} \slash dt = \frac{1}{3}$$ , find $$\mathit{dx} \slash dt$$ when $$x = 2$$ and $$y = 1$$ .
If $$\mathit{dx} \slash dt = 3$$ , find $$\mathit{dy} \slash dt$$ when $$x = - 2$$ and $$y = 1$$ .

problem.paragraph: If $$x^{2} + y^{2} + z^{2} = 9$$ , $$\mathit{dx} \slash dt = 5$$ , and $$\mathit{dy} \slash dt = 4$$ , find $$dz \slash dt$$ when $$\left( {x,y,z} \right) = \left( {2,2,1} \right)$$ .
The weight $$w$$ of an astronaut (in pounds) is related to her height $$w$$ above the surface of the earth (in miles) by

where $$w_{0}$$ is the weight of the astronaut on the surface of the earth. If the astronaut weighs $$130$$ pounds on earth and is in a rocket, being propelled upward at a speed of $$12{mi}/s$$ , find the rate at which her weight is changing (in lb/s) when she is $$40$$ miles above the earth’s surface.

A particle is moving along a hyperbola $$xy = 8$$ . As it reaches the point $$\left( {4,2} \right)$$ , the $$y$$ -coordinate is decreasing at a rate of $$3{cm} \slash s$$ . How fast is the $$x$$ -coordinate of the point changing at that instant?

list.item: What quantities are given in the problem?
What is the unknown?
Draw a picture of the situation for any time $$t$$ .
Write an equation that relates the quantities.
Finish solving the problem.

problem.paragraph: A plane flying horizontally at an altitude of $$1$$ mi and a speed of $$500{{mi} \slash h}$$ passes directly over a radar station. Find the rate at which the distance from the plane to the station is increasing when the plane is $$2$$ mi away from the station.

list.item: The plane’s altitude is $$1$$ mi and its speed is $$500{mi} \slash h$$ .
The rate at which the distance from the plane to the station is increasing when the plane is $$2$$ mi from the station
$$250\sqrt{3} \approx 433{mi} \slash h$$

problem.paragraph: If a snowball melts so that its surface area decreases at a rate of $$1{{cm}^{2} \slash \min}$$ , find the rate at which the diameter decreases when the diameter is $$10$$ cm.

A street light is mounted at the top of a $$15$$ -ft-tall pole. A man $$6$$ ft tall walks away from the pole with a speed of $$5{{ft} \slash s}$$ along a straight path. How fast is the tip of his shadow moving when he is $$40$$ ft from the pole?

list.item: The height of the pole $$(15{ft})$$ , the height of the man $$(6{ft})$$ , and the speed of the man $$\left( {5{ft} \slash s} \right)$$
The rate at which the tip of the man’s shadow is moving when he is $$40$$ ft from the pole
$$\frac{25}{3}{ft} \slash s$$

problem.paragraph: At noon, ship A is $$150$$ km west of ship B. Ship A is sailing east at $$35{km} \slash h$$ and ship B is sailing north at $$25{km} \slash h$$ . How fast is the distance between the ships changing at 4:00 pm?

Two cars start moving from the same point. One travels south at $$60{mi} \slash h$$ and the other travels west at $$25{mi} \slash h$$ . At what rate is the distance between the cars increasing two hours later?

A spotlight on the ground shines on a wall $$12$$ m away. If a man $$2$$ m tall walks from the spotlight toward the building at a speed of $$1.6m \slash s$$ , how fast is the length of his shadow on the building decreasing when he is $$4$$ m from the building?

A man starts walking north at $$4{ft} \slash s$$ from a point $$P$$ . Five minutes later a woman starts walking south at $$5{ft} \slash s$$ from a point $$500$$ ft due east of $$P$$ . At what rate are the people moving apart $$15$$ min after the woman starts walking?
A baseball diamond is a square with side $$90$$ ft. A batter hits the ball and runs toward first base with a speed of $$24{ft} \slash s$$ .

list.item: At what rate is his distance from second base decreasing when he is halfway to first base?
At what rate is his distance from third base increasing at the same moment?

problem.paragraph: The altitude of a triangle is increasing at a rate of $$1{cm} \slash \min$$ while the area of the triangle is increasing at a rate of $$2{cm}^{2} \slash \min$$ . At what rate is the base of the triangle changing when the altitude is $$10$$ cm and the area is $$100{cm}^{2}$$ ?

A boat is pulled into a dock by a rope attached to the bow of the boat and passing through a pulley on the dock that is $$1$$ m higher than the bow of the boat. If the rope is pulled in at a rate of $$1m \slash s$$ , how fast is the boat approaching the dock when it is $$8$$ m from the dock?

image.alt: Details An illustration shows a boat being pulled by a rope into a dock. One end of the rope is tied to the bow of the boat, passing through the pulley on the dock.

exercises.paragraph: 23–24 Use the fact that the distance (in meters) a dropped stone falls after $$t$$ seconds is $$d = 4.9t^{2}$$ .

problem.paragraph: A woman stands near the edge of a cliff and drops a stone over the edge. Exactly one second later she drops another stone. One second after that, how fast is the distance between the two stones changing?

Two men stand $$10$$ m apart on level ground near the edge of a cliff. One man drops a stone and one second later the other man drops a stone. One second after that, how fast is the distance between the two stones changing?

Water is leaking out of an inverted conical tank at a rate of $$10,000{cm}^{3} \slash \min$$ at the same time that water is being pumped into the tank at a constant rate. The tank has height $$6$$ m and the diameter at the top is $$4$$ m. If the water level is rising at a rate of $$20{cm} \slash \min$$ when the height of the water is $$2$$ m, find the rate at which water is being pumped into the tank.

A particle moves along the curve $$y = 2\sin\left( {\pi x \slash 2} \right)$$ . As the particle passes through the point $$\left( {\frac{1}{3},1} \right)$$ , its $$x$$ -coordinate increases at a rate of $$\sqrt{10^{}}{cm} \slash s$$ . How fast is the distance from the particle to the origin changing at this instant?

A water trough is $$10$$ m long and a cross-section has the shape of an isosceles trapezoid that is $$30$$ cm wide at the bottom, $$80$$ cm wide at the top, and has height $$50$$ cm. If the trough is being filled with water at the rate of $$0.2m^{3} \slash \min$$ , how fast is the water level rising when the water is $$30$$ cm deep?

A trough is $$10$$ ft long and its ends have the shape of isosceles triangles that are $$3$$ ft across at the top and have a height of $$1$$ ft. If the trough is being filled with water at a rate of $$12{ft}^{3} \slash \min$$ , how fast is the water level rising when the water is $$6$$ inches deep?

Gravel is being dumped from a conveyor belt at a rate of $$30{ft}^{3} \slash \min$$ , and its coarseness is such that it forms a pile in the shape of a cone whose base diameter and height are always equal. How fast is the height of the pile increasing when the pile is $$10$$ ft high?

image.alt: Details An illustration shows gravel from the conveyor belt forming a conical pile on the horizontal ground such that the height and the base diameter of the cone are the same.

problem.paragraph: A swimming pool is $$20$$ ft wide, $$40$$ ft long, $$3$$ ft deep at the shallow end, and $$9$$ ft deep at its deepest point. A cross-section is shown in the figure. If the pool is being filled at a rate of $$0.8{ft}^{3} \slash \min$$ , how fast is the water level rising when the depth at the deepest point is $$5$$ ft?

image.alt: Details An illustration shows a trapezoidal swimming pool filled with water. The trapezoidal pool has a smaller lower base with an open top. The horizontal distance from the top left vertex of the trapezoid to the bottom left vertex is 6 feet. The horizontal distance between the bottom left vertex and the bottom right vertex, that is, the lower base is 12 feet. The horizontal distance from the bottom right vertex to the top right vertex of the trapezoid is 16 feet. The height of the trapezoid is 6 feet. From the top right vertex of the trapezoid, a line segment of length 6 units runs horizontally rightward such that the total length of the pool is 40 feet. From the right end of this horizontal segment and from the top left vertex of the trapezoid, a vertical line segment of length 3 units rises upward such that the total height of the pool is 9 units.

problem.paragraph: The sides of an equilateral triangle are increasing at a rate of $$10{cm} \slash \min$$ . At what rate is the area of the triangle increasing when the sides are $$30$$ cm long?

A kite $$100$$ ft above the ground moves horizontally at a speed of $$8{ft} \slash s$$ . At what rate is the angle between the string and the horizontal decreasing when $$200$$ ft of string has been let out?

A car is traveling north on a straight road at $$20m/s$$ and a drone is flying east at $$6m/s$$ at an elevation of $$25$$ m. At one instant the drone passes directly over the car. How fast is the distance between the drone and the car changing $$5$$ seconds later?
If the minute hand of a clock has length $$r$$ (in centimeters), find the rate at which it sweeps out area as a function of $$r$$ .
How fast is the angle between the ladder and the ground changing in Example 2 when the bottom of the ladder is $$6$$ ft from the wall?
According to the model we used to solve Example 2, what happens as the top of the ladder approaches the ground? Is the model appropriate for small values of $$y$$ ?

Boyle’s Law states that when a sample of gas is compressed at a constant temperature, the pressure $$P$$ and volume $$V$$ satisfy the equation $$PV = C$$ , where $$C$$ is a constant. Suppose that at a certain instant the volume is $$600{cm}^{3}$$ , the pressure is $$150$$ kPa, and the pressure is increasing at a rate of $$20{kPa} \slash \min$$ . At what rate is the volume decreasing at this instant?

A faucet is filling a hemispherical basin of diameter $$60$$ cm with water at a rate of $$2L \slash \min$$ . Find the rate at which the water is rising in the basin when it is half full. [Use the following facts: $$1$$ L is $$1000{cm}^{3}$$ . The volume of the portion of a sphere with radius $$r$$ from the bottom to a height $$h$$ is $$V = \pi\left( {rh^{2} - \frac{1}{3}h^{3}} \right)$$ , as we will show in Chapter 6.]
If two resistors with resistances $$R_{1}$$ and $$R_{2}$$ are connected in parallel, as shown in the figure, then the total resistance $$R$$ , measured in ohms $$(\Omega)$$ , is given by

If $$R_{1}$$ and $$R_{2}$$ are increasing at rates of $$0.3\Omega \slash s$$ and $$0.2\Omega \slash s$$ , respectively, how fast is $$R$$ changing when $$R_{1} = 80\Omega$$ and $$R_{2} = 100\Omega$$ ?

image.alt: Details A closed-circuit consists of a resistor of resistance R_1 in the middle connected in parallel with a resistor of resistance R_2 on the right end. These two resistors are connected in parallel to a battery on the left end.

problem.paragraph: When air expands adiabatically (without gaining or losing heat), its pressure $$P$$ and volume $$V$$ are related by the equation $$PV^{1.4} = C$$ , where $$C$$ is a constant. Suppose that at a certain instant the volume is $$400{cm}^{3}$$ and the pressure is $$80$$ kPa and is decreasing at a rate of $$10{kPa} \slash \min$$ . At what rate is the volume increasing at this instant?

Two straight roads diverge from an intersection at an angle of $$60^{{^\circ}}$$ . Two cars leave the intersection at the same time, the first traveling down one road at $$40{mi}/h$$ and the second traveling down the other road at $$60{mi}/h$$ . How fast is the distance between the cars changing after half an hour? [Hint: Use the Law of Cosines (Formula 21 in Appendix D).]

Brain weight $$B$$ as a function of body weight $$W$$ in fish has been modeled by the power function $$B = 0.007W^{2 \slash 3}$$ , where $$B$$ and $$W$$ are measured in grams. A model for body weight as a function of body length $$L$$ (measured in centimeters) is $$W = 0.12L^{2.53}$$ . If, over $$10$$ million years, the average length of a certain species of fish evolved from $$15$$ cm to $$20$$ cm at a constant rate, how fast was this species’ brain growing when its average length was $$18$$ cm?

Two sides of a triangle have lengths $$12$$ m and $$15$$ m. The angle between them is increasing at a rate of $$2^{{^\circ}} \slash \min$$ . How fast is the length of the third side increasing when the angle between the sides of fixed length is $$60^{{^\circ}}$$ ? [Hint:: Use the Law of Cosines (Formula 21 in Appendix D).]

Two carts, A and B, are connected by a rope $$39$$ ft long that passes over a pulley $$P$$ . (See the figure.) The point $$Q$$ is on the floor $$12$$ ft directly beneath $$P$$ and between the carts. Cart A is being pulled away from $$Q$$ at a speed of $$2{ft} \slash s$$ . How fast is cart B moving toward $$Q$$ at the instant when cart A is $$5$$ ft from $$Q$$ ?

image.alt: Details An illustration shows two carts A and B on the horizontal ground. Cart B is located to the right of cart A. These two carts are connected by a rope, running over the pulley P from horizontal support at the top. Point Q is on the horizontal ground directly below point P. The vertical distance from point P to point Q is 12 feet. Cart A is moving away from point Q and is represented by a left arrow. Cart B is moving toward point Q and is represented by another left arrow.

problem.paragraph: A television camera is positioned $$4000$$ ft from the base of a rocket launching pad. The angle of elevation of the camera has to change at the correct rate in order to keep the rocket in sight. Also, the mechanism for focusing the camera has to take into account the increasing distance from the camera to the rising rocket. Let’s assume the rocket rises vertically and its speed is $$600{ft} \slash s$$ when it has risen $$3000$$ ft.

list.item: How fast is the distance from the television camera to the rocket changing at that moment?
If the television camera is always kept aimed at the rocket, how fast is the camera’s angle of elevation changing at that same moment?

problem.paragraph: A lighthouse is located on a small island $$3$$ km away from the nearest point $$P$$ on a straight shoreline and its light makes four revolutions per minute. How fast is the beam of light moving along the shoreline when it is $$1$$ km from $$P$$ ?

A plane flies horizontally at an altitude of $$5$$ km and passes directly over a tracking telescope on the ground. When the angle of elevation is $$\pi \slash 3$$ , this angle is decreasing at a rate of $$\pi \slash 6{rad} \slash \min$$ . How fast is the plane traveling at that time?
A Ferris wheel with a radius of $$10$$ m is rotating at a rate of one revolution every $$2$$ minutes. How fast is a rider rising when his seat is $$16$$ m above ground level?

A plane flying with a constant speed of $$300{km} \slash h$$ passes over a ground radar station at an altitude of $$1$$ km and climbs at an angle of $$30^{{^\circ}}$$ . At what rate is the distance from the plane to the radar station increasing a minute later?

Two people start from the same point. One walks east at $$3{mi} \slash h$$ and the other walks northeast at $$2{mi} \slash h$$ . How fast is the distance between the people changing after $$15$$ minutes?

A runner sprints around a circular track of radius $$100$$ m at a constant speed of $$7m \slash s$$ . The runner’s friend is standing at a distance $$200$$ m from the center of the track. How fast is the distance between the friends changing when the distance between them is $$200$$ m?
The minute hand on a watch is $$8$$ mm long and the hour hand is $$4$$ mm long. How fast is the distance between the tips of the hands changing at one o’clock?

Suppose that the volume $$V$$ of a rolling snowball increases so that $$\mathit{dv}/\mathit{dt}$$ is proportional to the surface area of the snowball at time $$t$$ . Show that the radius $$r$$ increases at a constant rate, that is, $$\mathit{dr}/\mathit{dt}$$ is constant.
